properties.name: Amw (Monsoon with Short Dry Season)
properties.climatic_mechanism: Intense orographic lifting of moisture-laden Southwest Monsoon winds against the windward slopes of the Western Ghats; maritime location prevents extreme temperature variations.
properties.precipitation_regime: Torrential monsoon precipitation (>250–300 cm annually) between June and September; brief, mild dry period during winter.
properties.temperature_profile: Uniformly high temperatures year-round (annual mean >27°C); very low diurnal and annual temperature range.
properties.distinctive_features: Supports luxuriant tropical wet evergreen and semi-evergreen rainforests; heavy runoff leads to intense soil leaching and laterization.
properties.major_crops: Rice, Spices (Cardamom, Black Pepper), Rubber, Coconut, Coffee, Tea, Areca Nut

properties.name: As (Monsoon with Dry Summer)
properties.climatic_mechanism: Lies in the deep rain-shadow of the Western Ghats during the summer SW monsoon; receives peak rainfall from the retreating (North-East) monsoon depressions over the Bay of Bengal.
properties.precipitation_regime: Summer is markedly dry; major rainfall occurs between October and December (~75–100 cm), often accompanied by severe coastal cyclonic storms.
properties.temperature_profile: Warm and tropical throughout the year (mean >28°C); mild, humid winters with minimal thermal variation.
properties.distinctive_features: Unique inverted rainfall cycle in peninsular India where the primary agricultural season aligns with the retreating winter monsoon.
properties.major_crops: Rice (Samba crop), Groundnut, Pulses, Millets, Cotton, Sugarcane

properties.name: Aw (Tropical Savanna)
properties.sub_type: Tropical Wet and Dry / Savanna Type
properties.climatic_mechanism: Alternating influence of the summer Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) migration and dry winter continental air masses over the peninsular plateau.
properties.precipitation_regime: Moderate rainfall (75–150 cm) concentrated strictly within the SW monsoon months; prolonged and severe drought conditions through winter and spring.
properties.temperature_profile: High temperatures throughout the year; peak summer temperatures frequently cross 40°C in May before cooling monsoon rains arrive.
properties.distinctive_features: Covers the largest portion of the peninsular plateau; characterized by tropical dry and moist deciduous forests; highly susceptible to agricultural drought if the monsoon is delayed.
properties.major_crops: Cotton, Soybean, Jowar, Bajra, Groundnut, Pulses, Sugarcane, Tobacco

properties.name: Cwg (Monsoon with Dry Winter)
properties.climatic_mechanism: Continental interior regime fed by the Bay of Bengal branch of the SW monsoon in summer, with periodic winter cyclonic rain from Mediterranean Western Disturbances.
properties.precipitation_regime: Substantial summer rainfall (100–200 cm in the east, tapering to 60–75 cm in the west); dry, clear winters with light precipitation beneficial for Rabi crops.
properties.temperature_profile: Pronounced continental range: scorching summers (>42°C with dry, hot 'Loo' winds) contrasting with cold, foggy winters where minimums drop to 3–7°C.
properties.distinctive_features: Standard 'Ganga Type' climate; the letter 'g' signifies that the hottest month occurs prior to the summer monsoon (May/June); anchors India's most productive agricultural belt.
properties.major_crops: Wheat, Rice, Sugarcane, Mustard, Maize, Jute, Potato, Pulses

properties.name: BShw (Semi-Arid Steppe)
properties.climatic_mechanism: Present in two distinct belts: (1) the transition corridor between the Thar Desert and the northern plains, and (2) the leeward rain-shadow belt of the Western Ghats.
properties.precipitation_regime: Deficient and highly unreliable rainfall (30–65 cm annually); potential evapotranspiration far exceeds annual precipitation.
properties.temperature_profile: Mean annual temperatures exceed 18°C; intense summer heat (>40°C) with mild, dry winter months.
properties.distinctive_features: Vegetation consists of xerophytic scrub, open thorny woodland, and coarse steppe grasses; predominantly reliant on dryland farming and canal/tube-well irrigation.
properties.major_crops: Bajra, Jowar, Ragi, Guar, Pulses (Gram, Moong), Castor Seed, Groundnut, Cotton
states_covered: Interior rain-shadow tract of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh

properties.name: BWhw (Hot Desert)
properties.climatic_mechanism: Atmospheric subsidence in the subtropical high-pressure zone; vast distance from the Bay of Bengal monsoon and parallel orientation of the Aravalli range preventing orographic lift.
properties.precipitation_regime: Hyper-arid conditions with scant and irregular rainfall (<15–25 cm per year); sudden flash showers followed by long multi-year dry spells.
properties.temperature_profile: Extreme thermal regime: summer daytime highs often exceed 48°C with high diurnal drops at night; winter night temperatures can approach freezing point (0°C).
properties.distinctive_features: Shifting sand dunes (barchans), intense wind erosion, and high soil salinity; settled agriculture is viable only along dedicated canal corridors (e.g., Indira Gandhi Canal).
properties.major_crops: Bajra, Guar, Moth Bean, Irrigated Wheat, Mustard, Cotton, Date Palms

properties.name: Dfc (Cold Humid Winter with Short Summer)
properties.climatic_mechanism: High-altitude elevation in the Eastern Himalayas combined with perennial maritime moisture funneled through the Brahmaputra gorge.
properties.precipitation_regime: High annual precipitation (>200 cm); heavy pre-monsoon and monsoon downpours, transitioning to heavy winter snow and freezing rain at high passes.
properties.temperature_profile: Short, cool, humid summers (mean temperature <18°C) and long, severely cold, damp winters lasting over 5 months.
properties.distinctive_features: High cloud cover, dense alpine and sub-alpine coniferous forests (pines, firs, rhododendrons), high relative humidity year-round, and frequent landslides.
properties.major_crops: Maize, Barley, Buckwheat, Cardamom, Temperate Fruits (Kiwi, Apple, Orange), Potato

properties.name: Et (Tundra Type)
properties.climatic_mechanism: High elevations above the timberline in the Greater Himalayas; severe solar attenuation due to thin mountain air and high albedo from snowfields.
properties.precipitation_regime: Low absolute precipitation, mostly occurring as dry snow and blizzards during winter Western Disturbances; very low atmospheric humidity.
properties.temperature_profile: Short, cold summer where the warmest month averages between 0°C and 10°C; bitter, freezing winters plunging below -20°C.
properties.distinctive_features: Extends between the tree line and the permanent snow line; vegetation is restricted to alpine meadows (Bugyals), lichens, mosses, and dwarf junipers; permafrost terrain.
properties.major_crops: Transhumant pastoralism (Yak, Pashmina goat, Sheep rearing); minimal summer barley and buckwheat in sheltered micro-valleys

properties.name: E (Polar / Perpetual Snow)
properties.sub_type: Perpetual Frost / Ice Cap Mountain Climate
properties.climatic_mechanism: Extreme elevation (>4,500–5,000 m) in the Trans-Himalayan, Karakoram, and Zanskar ranges; deep rain-shadow isolation behind the main Himalayan wall creates a high-altitude cold desert.
properties.precipitation_regime: Extremely dry (<10 cm annually in cold desert plains like Ladakh); precipitation falls almost exclusively as powdery snow and rime.
properties.temperature_profile: Mean temperature of all months remains near or below freezing (0°C); winter minimums routinely drop below -35°C to -45°C (e.g., Dras).
properties.distinctive_features: Dominated by vast valley glaciers (Siachen, Baltoro), rock screes, and bare frost-shattered peaks; completely devoid of natural tree cover; settlements depend entirely on glacial meltwater.
properties.major_crops: Nomadic wool/pashmina pastoralism; restricted oasis cultivation of Barley, Peas, Apricots, and Sea Buckthorn along meltwater channels
states_covered: High mountain ranges of Jammu and Kashmir
Northern border peaks of Himachal Pradesh
